summary: Iteration 1 confirmed that a bitset-accelerated branch-and-bound (BnB) with degeneracy ordering and greedy coloring bounds achieves near-perfect scores (100 in best run, 99.345 consistently) on the Maximum Clique problem, substantially outperforming greedy-only (92.158). The remaining gap to a perfect 100 is likely due to one or two hard test cases where BnB either times out or narrowly misses the optimal clique.
key_points: h-main (BnB + bitset + degeneracy ordering) scored 100 in 2/3 runs and 99.345 consistently across 6 focused runs — CONFIRMED that BnB with proper engineering achieves ≥95.

h-control-negative (greedy with 5000 restarts) scored 92.158 — higher than the predicted <85 but consistently 7-8 points below BnB, confirming BnB's value. The magnitude prediction was off; random-restart greedy is stronger than expected on these graphs.

The critical engineering insight: bitset<1001> adjacency with bitwise AND for candidate intersection was the single largest speedup (80→99.345), more impactful than any algorithmic change to the search strategy.
Score variance (90 vs 100 across runs) correlates with system load hitting the 2.0s time limit. The 1850ms internal cutoff mitigates this but doesn't eliminate it entirely.

Next iteration should investigate: (1) tighter time management per BnB subtree to avoid timeouts on hard cases, (2) complement-graph approach for very dense test instances, (3) local search (tabu or penalty-based) as a fallback when BnB is pruned by the time limit — targeting the last 0-1% improvement.
